paragraphs.notes: Markush enumeration table, recorded as one entry per the pass instructions. The en field is identical to the zh field: every cell is a chemical symbol or a compound number, and the only German-language token on the page is the column head 'Nr.' (Nummer, i.e. No.), which is left as printed so the header row matches the source. The table continues from the preceding page and continues onto the next: it opens mid-sequence at Nr. 233 with no Tabelle caption and no repeated caption row on this page, so the shared substituents fixed by that caption (and the drawn scaffold it belongs to) are not visible here and are not reproduced. The column heads are printed with superscripts, R with a raised 7a, 7b, 12 and 1; they are transcribed inline as R7a, R7b, R12, R1. Likewise the subscript digits in SO2, CH2CH2, OCH2CF3 and PhC(O)CH2 are printed as true subscripts and transcribed inline. The R12 cell of Nr. 241 is set one space further right than the PhSO2 entries above and below it; that is print alignment, not a different value, and the leading space is not carried into the transcription. A small ink blot sits directly above the O of O-c-Pr in the R1 cell of Nr. 234, touching the top of the letter but not obscuring it; the O and the rest of the cell are fully legible. Small stray dots sit in the Nr. cell of 234, the Nr. cell of 253 and the R7a cell of 255. All four marks read as scan artifacts rather than characters. The table body ends after Nr. 259 and the lower quarter of the page is blank.
